title: How Dogs and Humans Have Been Changing Each Other for 15,000 Years
summary: Did you know that dogs and humans have been best friends for over 15,000 years? A new book by archaeologist Peter Mitchell, called 'First Dogs,' tells the amazing story of how we changed each other. It wasn't just humans taming wolves. Mitchell thinks wolves and people started hanging out as equals. Over time, dogs became super different depending on where they lived. In the freezing Arctic, dogs became strong and fluffy to pull sleds across ice. Their bones show signs of heavy work, and they ate the same seafood as their human families. On the high Tibetan Plateau, both dogs and people developed special genes to breathe in thin air! In hot rainforests, dogs stayed smaller and quicker to hunt through thick plants. Some communities even bred dogs for their woolly hair to make blankets. Dogs also became part of our stories and religions. Today, we have everything from tiny Chihuahuas to giant Great Danes. All that variety came from thousands of years of living and working together. So next time you play with your dog, remember — you're part of a friendship that's older than any city or country!
why_it_matters: Every time you toss a ball for your dog, you’re part of a 15,000-year-old team that helped shape human history, from how we traveled to how we told stories.

background_read: Long ago, wolves started living near people and, over many generations, turned into the first dogs – the very first animal humans ever tamed.
Archaeologist Peter Mitchell (who studies ancient bones and objects left by early people) wrote the book 'First Dogs' to tell this long friendship story.
Today, there are over 340 dog breeds, from tiny Chihuahuas to huge Great Danes, all because thousands of years of working together shaped them in different ways.
Article_Structure: WHO: Archaeologist Peter Mitchell and the ancient humans and dogs that lived together.
WHAT: The book 'First Dogs' explains how dogs and people changed each other forever, with dogs helping humans survive in many harsh places.
WHERE: The story takes place all over the world, in the Arctic, the high Tibetan Plateau, and dense rainforests.
WHY: To show that the bond between us and dogs is very old and deep, and it helped make both humans and dogs the way we are today.

perspectives.description: I love knowing my dog is part of such an old story—it makes our friendship feel even more important, like we’re continuing something that started before cities existed.
Dogs helped humans hunt, guard camps, and pull heavy loads, which let people spread to every corner of the planet. Without dogs, history would look very different.

perspectives.perspective: Someone who cares about animal fairness
perspectives.description: While many call it a friendship, some people wonder if early wolves really had a choice, or if humans forced them into a life of work for our own benefit.
